newPageBriefs.contributionAndEvidence: Calculated (Phase 3 executes the calculator code and saves evidence.json with replay). Formula: net earnings = profit - half SE tax (IRS Pub 560 rate worksheet, saved); SEP = min(20% x net earnings, 415(c) cap); solo = min(employee deferral limit + 20% x net earnings, cap) + catch-up outside the cap. Limits from IRS Notice 2026-66 and IR-2026-136 (saved, retrieved 2026-11-25): 2027 deferral $25,500, catch-up $8,500, 60-63 $11,750, 415(c) $75,000, comp limit $375,000; 2026 $24,500 / $8,000 / $72,000 / $360,000. Example (research/calc-examples.json): $100,000 profit -> SE tax $14,130, SEP $18,587, solo 401(k) $44,087, +$8,500 at 50+. Counterexample: below about $18,000 net earnings a SEP is capped by the 20% rule while the solo deferral is not. 2027 SS wage base not asserted (see exclusions).
newPageBriefs.tablesToolsVisuals: Interactive calculator (React island; calc-ui components; data-tool=sep-ira-solo-401k-contribution-calculator; <=30 KB gz). Inputs: profit, tax year, age band, other deferrals; outputs: two plan maximums, difference, cap flags; export/print result. Sourced constants named in the lib with IRS URLs. Table of limits 2026 vs 2027 below the tool.
newPageBriefs.testingAndReview: Testing excluded (financial/tax guidance; _experience.md section G covers products/models, never financial services). Ordinary presentation, operator register with the editorial 'we', existing ModernWallet Research Desk byline and publisher/editorial reviewer note per _experience.md (register-reviewer-note in Phase 3); YMYL disclaimer at the bottom via template; HIGH review profile because consequential tax/retirement claims; no professionalReviewRequired flag, but the page says to confirm with a tax professional for unusual situations. Attribution: 'In our internal calculation, we modeled ...' beside the worked example, never 'we tested'.
newPageBriefs.takeaway: For most sole proprietors a solo 401(k) allows far more than a SEP at the same profit because the $25,500 employee deferral sits on top of the 20% employer share; at high profit both hit the $75,000 cap and a SEP is simpler. The answer changes for anyone with employees (SEP must cover them) or W-2 deferrals elsewhere that use up the employee limit.

readerAndAnswer.question: How much of my stock losses can I deduct this year and carry forward? [PAA 2/6 on-topic: 'How do I find out if I have capital loss carryover?', 'What are the rules for carry forward of losses?'; ac 14 how/what questions; 4/6 PAA tax-rate off-topic]
readerAndAnswer.answer: Losses first cancel gains; a net loss deducts at most $3,000 ($1,500 married filing separately) against other income and the rest carries forward indefinitely (IRS Topic 409); a $50,000 net loss with no gains takes about 16 years to use.
